text: The Patriots' catastrophic 1-2 start has devolved into a crisis of both personnel and performance, with the offense dead last in the NFL at 9.7 points per game after Sunday's 35-6 demolition by Jacksonville—a game in which Drake Maye threw two interceptions and lost a fumble before acknowledging that the unit's play was simply "unacceptable." While Maye insisted Wednesday that his right shoulder hasn't impacted his throwing ability and expressed confidence in working with Mike Vrabel, the quarterback is clearly searching for answers within himself rather than blaming physical limitations, even as the infrastructure around him crumbles: the Patriots placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve Tuesday due to a thigh injury, and subsequently signed rookie offensive lineman Da'Metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad in a scramble to shore up the line. The week culminates with New England traveling to Buffalo on Sunday at 1 PM ET to face the Bills at Highmark Stadium, a road game that arrives amid questions about whether the Patriots are deploying Maye correctly and whether this offensive scheme can be salvaged before the season slips further away.
